sections.h2: Where can you reach Guilford County's recording office, and what are its hours?
sections.html:
There are two counters. Greensboro is at 201 W. Market St., with real estate and recording upstairs on the second floor. High Point is at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. One number, 336-641-7556, serves both, and staff work weekdays from 8 until 5.

Mail can be addressed to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. Rowan and Orange counties gave up land to form Guilford in 1771, and one set of land records now covers a Jamestown farmhouse, a Summerfield lot and a downtown Greensboro condo alike. General questions can go to guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov, and the Census Bureau counted 562,234 residents in mid-2025.

sections.h2: What is the process for filing a deed with Guilford County?
sections.html:
Deliver a properly formatted deed with the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office puts it on record. Electronic submission works too, because Guilford accepts every real estate document sent through its approved e-recording vendors.

E-recording returns the book and page data plus a stamped image within minutes, and the system rejects a document immediately if it misses the state's recording standards. Paper filings must also show where to send the original after recording. The county's checklist for a standard document includes:

  • Letter or legal size paper, one-sided, black type on white stock.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and a quarter inch of margin elsewhere.
  • Type no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument's title printed as a heading on the first sheet.
  • Pen entries for blanks and corrections are acceptable.

A document that fails any item draws the non-standard surcharge on top of the regular fee, so check the layout before you send it.

sections.h2: What fees does the Guilford County recording office collect?
sections.html:
Pricing starts at $26 for a general instrument of up to 15 pages, and a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages starts at $64. Each page beyond those limits adds $4. State law fixes those amounts, and the county's published table adds the smaller line items.

Guilford County Register of Deeds fee schedule, recording and copies
ItemFee printed by the county
Deed or other instrument$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Non-standard document$25 on top of the recording fee
Each added instrument in one document$10
Satisfaction of security instrumentNo fee
Plat or condominium map recording$21 per page
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page

Source: the county's Recording and Real Estate page. An ordinary copy of a real estate record is 5 cents a page at the counter and $1 by mail. Under the statute these fees are the only ones allowed, and payment comes first.

The county's page lists a few extras that come up around a sale. A notary oath costs $10, and authenticating a notary costs $1 per notary per page. A map copy is 50 cents, and certified plats are $5 per copy. UCC filings run $38, or $45 above two pages plus $2 for each page past ten. The Guilford office takes only fixture-related UCC filings, and every other UCC filing goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

sections.h2: Who pays the Guilford County deed excise tax?
sections.html:
The transferor does, handing it to the register before the deed goes on record. State law sets the rate at $1 per $500 of the price, counting any leftover fraction as a full $500, and the county's table shows deeds since August 1, 1991 at $2 per thousand, which is the same thing.

Half of the revenue stays in the county's general fund and the remainder is forwarded each month to the state revenue department. A closing statement lists the tax apart from the recording fee. The county's table also carries two older rate bands, $1 per thousand for 1968 through July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968, which matter only when you read an old deed. For your own sale, get the exact figure from the closing attorney.

sections.h2: What happens to a payoff after it is recorded in Guilford County?
sections.html:
The loan stays visible against the title until someone records a satisfaction. North Carolina gives an unrecorded deed, option or long lease no priority over lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and ranks competing claims by when they were registered.

Guilford describes three recordable forms of satisfaction, none of which costs anything to file:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and acknowledged before a notary.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit by a North Carolina attorney serving as satisfaction agent, for use when a lender never provides one.

The office stopped taking the original deed of trust and note as proof of payment. If an old lender's loan still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears it, and your attorney or the lender can arrange that.

sections.h2: How should Guilford County owners protect against forged deeds?
sections.html:
Enroll in the Property Fraud Alert. It emails notice when a document appears under a name variation you registered. The register must record a deed that meets the legal form once fees and taxes are paid, and the office does not test whether a signature is real.

The county names vacant or distressed homes, older owners and low-income owners as frequent targets. Its warning signs include a transfer you never signed, tax bills that stop arriving, and a default notice on a home with no mortgage. An owner who finds a bad deed should assemble the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney and the register. The register cannot pull a recorded document from the index, so ask an attorney how to challenge it.

The county also advises checking credentials, reading contracts and considering a title search and title insurance.

sections.h2: Can the Guilford County register correct a mistake in a recorded deed?
sections.html:
Only indexing mistakes. G.S. 132-1.10 bars the office from changing a recorded instrument, so a misspelled name, a faulty legal description or a wrong loan amount in the document itself needs a corrective instrument prepared by your attorney.

The Indexing Correction Request form handles cases where the index differs from the document. Call 336-641-7556 or use the office email with questions. The corrective instrument is recorded at the usual fees. The recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

sections.h2: How does Guilford County's housing stock look in the Census data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts counts 246,403 housing units for July 2025. For 2020 through 2024, the survey puts a middle-priced owned home at $259,900, the owner share of occupied homes at 59.9%, and median gross rent at $1,163.

The county's middle household earns $68,642 in 2024 dollars, and builders pulled 2,876 permits in 2025. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches Guilford's register of deeds?
faqs.a: 336-641-7556, for the Greensboro office at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Staff are available on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

faqs.q: What does a Guilford deed filing cost?
faqs.a: Expect $26 for an instrument of up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past that, plus a $25 surcharge when the document is non-standard. The seller also pays the excise tax before recording.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available through the Guilford register?
faqs.a: Yes. The office takes all electronically submitted real estate documents via approved vendors, sends back the recording details and a stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state standards.

faqs.q: Does the Guilford register verify a deed's authenticity?
faqs.a: No. A deed that meets the format rules is recorded once fees and taxes are paid. Owners can sign up for the free Property Fraud Alert and report forgeries to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

faqs.q: Do satisfactions of a mortgage carry a Guilford recording fee?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are filed free of charge. The office does not accept the original deed of trust and note in their place.
